title: NEB Class 11 Chemistry — Hydrocarbons — 2024
subject: chemistry
source: NEB Grade 11 Model Questions / NEB Past Papers 2020-2024

questions.question: How is ethane prepared from ethene? Write the reaction mechanism.
questions.solution:
**Catalytic hydrogenation:** CH₂=CH₂ + H₂ → CH₃–CH₃ (Ni/Pt catalyst, ~200°C).

**Mechanism:** (1) H₂ adsorbs and dissociates on the metal surface; (2) ethene adsorbs via its π-bond; (3) H atoms add stepwise to the carbons; (4) ethane desorbs.
questions.knowledgeNote: Addition (alkenes) vs substitution (alkanes) is the reactivity divide of the whole unit.

questions.question: State Markovnikov's rule and apply it to the addition of HBr to propene.
questions.solution:
**Markovnikov:** the H of HX adds to the doubly-bonded carbon already richer in H.

CH₃–CH=CH₂ + HBr → **CH₃–CHBr–CH₃ (2-bromopropane)** — H goes to C-1, Br to the more stable secondary carbocation at C-2.
questions.knowledgeNote: Carbocation stability (3° > 2° > 1°) is the reason behind the rule — peroxides flip it (Kharasch effect).

questions.question: How is ethane prepared by the Wurtz reaction? Write the chemical equation.
questions.solution:
Alkyl halides couple with sodium in dry ether: **2CH₃Br + 2Na → CH₃–CH₃ + 2NaBr**.

Best for symmetric alkanes — mixed halides give product mixtures.
questions.knowledgeNote: Dry ether is essential — water would destroy the organosodium intermediates.

questions.question: What happens when ethene undergoes ozonolysis? Write the products.
questions.solution:
O₃ adds across the double bond (ozonide), and reductive work-up (Zn/H₂O) cleaves it:

CH₂=CH₂ → **2HCHO (formaldehyde)**.

Ozonolysis locates double bonds — each =CH₂ fragment reports as formaldehyde.
questions.knowledgeNote: Oxidative work-up instead gives acids — the work-up reagent picks the product family.

questions.question: Acetylene is acidic in nature. Explain with a chemical test.
questions.solution:
The sp-hybridised C–H bond (50% s-character) holds electrons tightly, so HC≡CH loses H⁺ relatively easily.

**Test:** with ammoniacal AgNO₃ it gives a **white precipitate of silver acetylide** (AgC≡CAg); with ammoniacal Cu₂Cl₂ a red copper acetylide — terminal alkynes only.
questions.knowledgeNote: Acidity: acetylene > ethylene > ethane — s-character order (50% > 33% > 25%).

questions.question: How will you distinguish ethane, ethene, and ethyne using bromine water?
questions.solution: **Ethane:** no change (alkane, substitution needs UV). **Ethene:** brown Br₂ water decolourised (addition). **Ethyne:** also decolourised — then apply ammoniacal AgNO₃, which precipitates only with the terminal alkyne.
questions.knowledgeNote: Decolourisation = unsaturation (C=C or C≡C) — the fastest functional-group screen in qualitative analysis.
